skill.description: Deploy containerized frontend and backend applications to Azure Container Apps using remote builds, managed identities, Bicep, and repeatable Azure Developer CLI workflows.
skill.summary: Guide repeatable Azure Container Apps deployments with azd, Bicep, managed identity, service discovery, and deployment hooks.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: No prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or Ruby backtick execution was found; most static alerts are Markdown formatting or documented Azure paths. Confirmed risks include a predictable temporary file, suppressed RBAC failures, and environment commands that can expose secrets. The affected examples require hardening before publication.

remediation.issue: Secrets can appear in command arguments, terminal output, or shell history.
remediation.suggestion: Use Azure Key Vault and managed identity for secrets. Avoid displaying all environment values, redact logs, and require protected local environment files.

remediation.issue: RBAC assignment errors are redirected and ignored.
remediation.suggestion: Remove unconditional `2>/dev/null || true`. Handle only verified duplicate assignments and stop deployment when authorization or scope validation fails.

remediation.issue: Deployment hooks share the predictable `/tmp/domains.json` path.
remediation.suggestion: Create a private file with `mktemp`, restrict permissions, validate ownership, and remove it with a trap after the same deployment run.

content.user_title: Deploy Azure Container Apps Reliably with azd
content.value_statement: Azure Container Apps deployments often require coordinated infrastructure, builds, identities, and configuration. This skill provides focused azd and Bicep patterns for repeatable deployments.
actual_capabilities: Explains minimal and multi-service azure.yaml configurations for Azure Container Apps.
Maps azd environment values into Bicep parameters and deployment outputs.
Shows remote container build settings for frontend and backend services.
Provides Bicep patterns for existing resources, internal service discovery, and managed identity.
Demonstrates preprovision, postprovision, and postdeploy hook structures.
Lists common azd commands for provisioning, deployment, environment management, status, and logs.
limitations: The skill provides guidance and examples; it does not execute or verify deployments automatically.
Examples require project-specific names, resource identifiers, regions, roles, and access policies.
Users need authenticated Azure Developer CLI and Azure CLI sessions with appropriate permissions.
Temporary-file and RBAC error-handling examples require security hardening before production use.

use_cases.title: Bootstrap a container service
use_cases.description: Structure a Python or TypeScript service for remote builds and Azure Container Apps deployment.

use_cases.title: Standardize platform deployments
use_cases.description: Define repeatable Bicep, managed identity, RBAC, and environment patterns across deployment stages.

use_cases.title: Review release automation
use_cases.description: Assess azd hooks, service discovery, existing resources, and deployment commands before a production release.

prompt_templates.title: Create a minimal service plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a minimal azure.yaml plan for my Python backend on Azure Container Apps. Use remote builds and list required inputs before deployment.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one containerized backend service.

prompt_templates.title: Design a full application layout
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an azd layout for TypeScript frontend and Python backend services. Include Bicep modules, internal service discovery, and environment variable flow.
prompt_templates.scenario: Plan a two-service application with shared infrastructure.

prompt_templates.title: Add managed identity and RBAC
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt my Bicep deployment for system-assigned managed identity and least-privilege RBAC. Identify every required resource ID and role.
prompt_templates.scenario: Replace application credentials with Azure identity.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a production deployment
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my azd configuration for idempotency, domain preservation, secret exposure, temporary-file safety, and RBAC errors. Propose changes before running commands.
prompt_templates.scenario: Review an advanced deployment before production release.

output_examples.input: Plan a minimal deployment for one Python API.
output: A project layout covering the service, Dockerfile, azure.yaml, and Bicep infrastructure.
A list of Azure inputs, authentication requirements, and deployment stages.
A validation checklist for remote build and Container Apps health.

output_examples.input: Review my frontend and backend deployment design.
output_examples.output: A structured review identifies service boundaries, internal routing, environment flow, identity roles, idempotency risks, and changes required before deployment.

output_examples.input: Plan managed identity access to Azure OpenAI and Azure AI Search.
output: Required system-assigned identity outputs and resource scopes.
Least-privilege role assignments for each Azure service.
Failure checks that preserve RBAC errors instead of hiding them.

best_practices: Review the Azure subscription, environment, region, resource names, and estimated impact before provisioning.
Keep secrets in Azure Key Vault and use managed identity instead of command-line secret values.
Test idempotency, hook failure behavior, and rollback procedures in a nonproduction environment.
anti_patterns: Do not run azd up without confirming the selected subscription and environment.
Do not suppress every RBAC error or treat failed authorization as a successful deployment.
Do not store deployment state in predictable shared temporary files.

faq.question: Does this skill deploy resources automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides deployment guidance and command examples. Execution requires an authenticated user or agent with explicit Azure permissions.

faq.question: Which Azure services does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Azure Container Apps, Azure Container Registry remote builds, Bicep infrastructure, managed identity, and Azure RBAC.

faq.question: Can it support frontend and backend services?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples cover separate frontend and backend services with internal service discovery and independent container build contexts.

faq.question: How should secrets be handled?
faq.answer: Use Azure Key Vault and managed identity. Avoid command arguments, terminal output, source control, and unprotected environment files for secret values.

faq.question: Are azd deployments always idempotent?
faq.answer: Bicep reconciles declared resources, but hooks and manually configured resources can introduce side effects. Test repeated deployments before production use.

faq.question: Why use remote container builds?
faq.answer: Remote builds reduce local architecture differences and use Azure Container Registry build infrastructure. They still require valid Docker contexts and permissions.
